Decision written to review/A-evidence-1/decision.json: PROMOTE.

Facts (each is a claim in the file with a verified query):
- Zero 5xx on both versions; all 9819 requests returned 200 (stable 7343, canary 2476).
- Canary latency was elevated only in the first 30 s: canary p95=210 ms vs stable p95=93 ms.
- From t>=60 s the canary matches stable: canary p95=94 ms / p99=104 ms vs stable p95=95 ms / p99=104 ms.
- Steady-state per path is also equal: /browse 27 vs 27 ms p95, /search 59 vs 59 ms p95, /checkout 103 vs 104 ms p95.

Judgement: the only degradation is a transient warm-up on the single freshly started canary pod (first ~30 s), it decays monotonically across the 30 s windows and is gone by 60 s, with no error-rate impact at all. That is a start-up cost, not a regression, so promoting is low risk; a rollback here would block a release over warm-up noise. Residual risk (judgement): the canary carried only ~25% of traffic from one pod, so this test does not prove behaviour at 4x load — recommend promoting with a staged rollout and watching p95/5xx as replicas scale.

Note on tooling: pct(numbers, p) in run_query takes p as a fraction (pct(ms,0.95)); passing 95 returns the max. All claim queries use the fraction form and reproduce the dashboard numbers.
